'''''Serruria rosea''''', the '''rose spiderhead''', is a flower-bearing [[shrub]] that belongs to the [[genus]] ''[[Serruria]]'' and forms part of the [[fynbos]]. The plant is native to the [[Western Cape]], [[South Africa]].<ref name="sanbi">{{cite web|title=Serruria rosea {{!}} PlantZAfrica|url=http://pza.sanbi.org/serruria-rosea|access-date=12 December 2021|website=pza.sanbi.org}}</ref>

==Description==
Fire destroys the plant but the seeds survive. Two months after flowering, the fruit falls off and ants disperse the seeds. They store the seeds in their nests. The plant is [[Plant reproductive morphology|bisexual]]. Pollination takes place through the action of insects. The shrub is erect and grows {{Convert|0.8|-|1|m|abbr=on}} tall and bears flowers from August to October.<ref name="sanbi" />

In Afrikaans, it is known as the {{Lang|af|Bruidsbos}}.

==Distribution and habitat==
The plant only occurs in the [[Hottentots Holland Mountains]] from [[Slanghoek Mountains]] to [[Franschhoek]]. It grows in sandy soil at altitudes of {{Convert|300|-|620|m|abbr=on}}.
